issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" entry in the error message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple lists "transcriber_error" twice. Harmless to set-membership semantics, but it is a clear sign the list was hand-built without an audit. A reader pauses here. Make the membership test a frozenset literal at module scope, named like ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES, with one entry per error and a comment citing the ElevenLabs error-handling doc.

issues.description: Loop invariant of _receive_messages is no longer stated, and silent termination is now the contract
issues.detail: Previously the outer try/except made the termination condition explicit: any exception ends the receive loop and the caller reconnects. After the change, _receive_messages terminates whenever the async-for iterator stops, with no comment stating that invariant. A one-line literate comment ("loop exits when the websocket iterator closes; the outer reconnect loop in websocket_service handles resumption") would make the fix self-evidencing.

issues.description: Inner per-message try/except still swallows all exceptions, including the ones that should terminate the loop
issues.detail: The per-message handler catches bare Exception and logs at error level. That means a programming bug in _process_response (KeyError, AttributeError) is indistinguishable from a malformed frame, and the loop continues. Narrow the except to json.JSONDecodeError (already handled) plus a documented set, or re-raise on unexpected types so the websocket_service reconnect path can do its job.

issues.description: Error payload key may not be "error" for every new message_type; fallback message can be misleading
issues.detail: data.get("error", f"Unknown error - {message_type}") assumes every variant uses the "error" field. ElevenLabs docs show varied shapes (e.g., quota and rate-limit frames carry structured fields). Without auditing each schema, the user-visible message will silently degrade to "Unknown error - rate_limited" even when a descriptive field exists. Worth a brief per-type mapping or at least a TODO citing the doc revision audited.

issues.description: Lost log line: prior code logged ElevenLabs errors at error level; new code only push_errors
issues.detail: The old branches did logger.error(...) and push_error(...). The consolidated branch drops the logger.error call, leaving only push_error. Whether downstream consumers of error frames also log them is not obvious from this diff. A single logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}") preserves operator visibility without cost.
changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline (\ No newline at end of file). Minor, but most lint tooling and POSIX text-file conventions expect one. Trivial fix.

review.summary: The fix is directionally correct: removing the outer try/except in _receive_messages lets the websocket_service reconnect loop see the disconnect instead of swallowing it, breaking the infinite-loop pathology. The widened error-type handling is also welcome. UNDER-AUDITED on three fronts: the message_type tuple has a duplicate entry and no documented source-of-truth, the inner per-message handler still catches bare Exception (which can mask the very class of bugs that motivated the outer removal), and the new termination contract of _receive_messages is implicit where a one-line literate comment would make it explicit. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT, not WRONG. Address the duplicate, narrow the inner except, and state the loop invariant; the rest is polish.
